question: Does the atlas (structural-NN mechanism transfer) add value over the cheap baseline (sequence-NN transfer to the same M-CSA reference set)? Run on the independent gold held-out (EC-derived labels).
design: Same nearest-neighbour-transfer paradigm, two distance metrics: STRUCTURE (foldseek TM vs 133 atlas members, gate 0.70) vs SEQUENCE (best Smith-Waterman/BLOSUM62 hit among the same members, BLAST-like). Truth = experimental EC, independent of both. Apples-to-apples.

discrimination_failsafe.note: OOS = 72 enzymes outside all covered families (methyltransferase/glycosidase/isomerase/ligase). Can each method tell 'covered' from 'not'?
discrimination_failsafe.interpretation: OOS enzymes are as sequence-similar to atlas members (median 0.34) as the in-scope ones (0.39), so sequence identity CANNOT separate covered from non-covered. The atlas's structural TM gate abstains on 70/72. Structure discriminates; sequence does not.

verdict.value_proven_twilight_zone: At 25-40% identity (homology twilight), atlas recovers 0.70 vs sequence-NN 0.28 - a ~2.5x advantage where sequence transfer becomes unreliable.
verdict.value_proven_failsafe: Atlas abstains on out-of-family enzymes (2/72 FP) that are sequence-indistinguishable from covered ones - a discrimination sequence-NN cannot do at any threshold.
verdict.NOT_proven_orphan_recovery: 0/45 atlas-recovered proteins were sequence-orphans (all had >=25% identity to some atlas member; recovered median identity 0.37). So the STRONGEST claim - structure assigns mechanism where sequence is fully blind - is NOT demonstrated by this gold set (it contains ~no orphans).
verdict.baseline_caveat: Baseline is pairwise BLAST-like NN, not a profile HMM (HMMER/Pfam). Profile methods detect remoter homology and could narrow the twilight-zone gap; the discrimination/fail-safe result would likely persist and is the stronger finding.
